title: Network Systems Technician
raw_text:
8-255N. MOS 255N--Network Systems Technician
  a. Licensing/certification requirement. CompTIA Security+ CE or DOD 8570.01-M IAT Level II and IAM
Level I certifications.
  b. Prerequisites. DA PAM 611-21.
  c. MOS 255N. MOS 255N is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is any MOS. All enlisted
MOS to include other military services who can substantiate their qualifications with performance
evaluations, awards, and certificates in the Information Technology (IT) field in voice and data
internetworking, local and wide area networks (LAN & WAN), include terrestrial, satellite and aerial
systems and/or network planning as assessed through the accession process meets current
requirements.
  d. Associated SQIs.
      (1) 0--No special qualifications.
      (2) 8--Instruction.
      (3) P--Parachutiste.
      (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
      (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
  e. Associated ASIs. Refer to table 6-5 for listing of universal ASI’s associated with all warrant officer
MOS. 2Y Space Control Systems Operator (In Grade W2 only) (Effective 202410).
   f. Qualifications.
      (1) Physical Demands Category – Moderate (Gold).
      (2) WO1/CW2 must--
          (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
          (b) Must qualify for and maintain a Top Secret (TS) clearance with special compartmentalized
information (SCI) access. MOS 255N warrant officers will initiate procedures to obtain the proper level of
clearance immediately upon notification of the MOS 255N functional designation.
          (c) Meet vision and hearing standards of AR 40-501 for assignment of officers to Signal Corps,
normal color discrimination per AR 40-501, and have full use of both hands.
          (d) Successfully complete the MOS 255N Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC).
          (e) DoD 8570.01-M IAM Level II and Information Technology certifications in the routing and
switching environments are desired.
          (f) Minimum OPAT scores for physical demands category moderate (gold) are: Long Jump (LJ) -
0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic
Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles
       (3) CW3 must--
          (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (1).
          (b) CW2s assigned to CW3 positions will be a graduate of MOS 255N Warrant Officer Advance
Course (WOAC) prior to assignment.
           (c) DoD 8570.01-M CSSP Infrastructure Support and IAM Level III certifications are desired.
       (4) CW4 must--
            (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (2).
            (b) CW3s assigned to CW4 positions will be a graduate of the WOILE prior to assignment.
            (c) DoD 8570.01-M CSSP Infrastructure Support and IAM Level III certifications are desired.
        (5) CW5 must see MOS 255Z.
    g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2--
            (a) Designs, builds, configures, operates, maintains, and sustains voice, video, and data
networks within the Army’s portion of the cyberspace domain on the Department of Defense Information
Networks (DODIN).
           (b) Enables secure transmissions of networked information to support and enable mission
command.
            (c) Implements cybersecurity network policies and the use of electronic keys for transmission
systems.
            (d) Advises the commander or Signal operations officer of the status of assigned networks, sub-
networks, and associated systems.
            (e) May serve as a Network Systems Technician in a Brigade Combat Team, Multi-functional
Brigade, or Security Forces Assistance Brigade staff.
            (f) May serve as a Network Systems Technician in a Functional Support Brigade or
Expeditionary Signal Battalion staff, or Cyber Protection Team.
        (2) CW3--
            (a) Direct and performs duties described in paragraph g (1).
            (b) Trains and supervises cyberspace information technology personnel in the designing,
building, configuring, operating, maintaining, securing, and sustaining networks, network systems
equipment, network nodal devices, transmission and transport systems from the strategic level to the
tactical edge.
            (c) Leads frequency management to support communication networks.
            (d) Advises senior staff members, decision, and policy makers on communication networks and
transport systems operations, training, policies, and procedures.
            (e) May serve as a Network Systems Technician of Functional BDE, Division, WHCA, NIE, JTIC,
DISA staff or COCOM or ASCC Commander COMMO Team.
            (f) May serve as a Network Systems Technician at a Regional Hub Node or Regional Cyber
Center.
            (g) May serve as an Instructor/Writer, WOCC TAC officer, Training Center O/C.
            (h) May serve as senior Network Systems Technician in Nominative assignments.
            (i) May serve as the HRC SC Junior WO Assignments Manager.
       (3) CW4--
            (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (2).
            (b) Develops policy recommendations and provides technical guidance and advice to
commanders and staffs on the management and operation of Army, Joint, intergovernmental,
interagency, and multinational communication networks and transport systems.
            (c) May serve as senior Network Systems Technician of Functional BDE, JMC, TSOC, Corps
staff.
            (d) May serve as senior Network Systems Technician for DISA/COCOM/ACOM/ASCC/DRU
Staff.
            (e) May serve as senior Network Systems Technician for HQDA staff or in Nominative
Assignments.
             (f) May serve as the HRC SC Senior WO Assignments Manager.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
        (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
        (2) Table 8-255N-1. Physical requirements.
        (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of three definable skill levels: W2
equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; and W4 equals CW4. The grades are listed in the following
standards of grade tables:
             (a) Table 8-255N-1. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-255N-2. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
